text.p: Following are the main stories in Monday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Two more state executive councillors have been placed under investigation by the Anti-Corruption Agency, bringing to 10 the number now under full probe.
-- A six-month suspension of driving licenses is now in store for any driver caught for a second time holding a handphone while driving.
-- Half the manufacturing firms in a recent nationwide survey say they hedge their currency risks and do not need to pass on higher costs to consumers if the ringgit weakens.

-- Lityan Holdings Bhd expects to finalise its joint venture with Swiss company Ascom AG, a leading telecommunications player, to set up a research and development centre in the Multimedia Super Corridor by the end of the month.

-- Acting Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim may spring a pleasant surprise on the securities and fund management industry when he attends a dinner this Friday in conjunction with the Securities Commission (SC) dialogue with stockbrokers. Sources say he may announce new incentives to further liberalise Malaysia's capital markets.
